holidays.name: Squirrel Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A day to cheer for the acrobatic, nut-burying fluffballs in your backyard. Scatter some acorns, watch their daredevil leaps from branch to branch, and give these bushy-tailed neighbors a little respect.
holidays.origin: Christy Hargrove, a wildlife rehabilitator from North Carolina, created the observance, and it was first celebrated on January 21, 2002. She picked midwinter because squirrels are working hardest to find food then.
holidays.funFact: Squirrels forget where they buried many of their nuts, and the forgotten ones often sprout into new trees. That makes squirrels accidental forest planters.

holidays.name: National Hugging Day
holidays.description: A day for sharing warm hugs with friends, family, and anyone who is willing. It is meant to counter the winter blues with a little human contact, as long as the other person is comfortable with it.
holidays.origin: Kevin Zaborney started it in 1986 in Michigan. He chose a date between the holidays and Valentine's Day, when people's spirits tend to sag.
holidays.funFact: A hug can release oxytocin, often called the 'cuddle hormone.' That is why a good squeeze can feel like a mood boost.

holidays.name: National Granola Bar Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the humble, chewy, oat-packed snack that lives in backpacks, desk drawers, and glove compartments everywhere. Try a new flavor or make your own batch.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin that celebrates the portable snack bar.
holidays.funFact: Granola was invented in the 19th century as a health food. It was first made in New York in the 1860s and was originally a rock-hard baked cereal that had to be soaked overnight.
